hooks.text: A British commander ordered his own intelligence officer onto forced medical leave.
Why did a British commander send his top intelligence officer on forced leave?
Allied commanders launched history's largest drop but silenced their own scout.

title: Why Did Allies Ignore Arnhem's Panzer Warnings? ⚠️
description: In September 1944, Operation Market Garden ended in disaster after commanders dismissed clear aerial evidence of German tanks.

beats.text: A British commander ordered his own intelligence officer onto forced medical leave.
beats.visual: photograph of Lieutenant General Frederick Browning, 1944

beats.text: It was September 1944, just before Operation Market Garden launched.
beats.visual: Map of Operation Market Garden airborne corridor, 1944

beats.text: The officer had spotted German tanks waiting near Arnhem.
beats.visual: German armored vehicles during the Battle of Arnhem, 1944

beats.text: Commanders ignored the warning and proceeded with the massive drop.
queries: C-47 Dakota dropping paratroopers Operation Market Garden

beats.text: They dropped paratroopers directly onto elite German SS panzer divisions.
beats.visual: Airspeed Horsa gliders on Dutch landing zones near Arnhem, 1944

beats.text: The isolated troops were quickly overwhelmed, and the operation failed.

beats.text: They should have listened instead of forcing him onto medical leave.
